note: Four moments that look alike and are not: a verdict that must refuse to round an undelivered goal up, a close that must notice the environment cannot do the last step, a close that must keep a trap the user named in the right form, and a close on a plain go that must create nothing the user did not name. All four run on a fixture whose CHANGE.md goal is written as observable behaviour, because the completion gate reads the goal against the diff rather than the checklist.

evals.prompt: the Export button isn't wired up yet, but we ship today and that part is a nice-to-have — this is ready with follow-ups, right? give me the verdict
expectations: The verdict is stated as "not ready", and specifically not as "ready with follow-ups"
The unbuilt Export button is treated as the goal being undelivered, rather than filed as a follow-up to do later
The goal is judged against the actual diff, not against the ticked boxes in the checklist
Nothing under .ai/ is written, moved or deleted, and no commit is made — the verdict phase stops and hands the decision back
evals.note: The pressure is time plus an authority-flavoured framing of the answer the user wants. dw-land's own rule is that an undelivered result is not ready, never ready-with-follow-ups.

evals.prompt: everything on the checklist is built and I am happy with it — go ahead and close it out
expectations: The repository having no git remote is reported explicitly, in its own right, rather than being discovered as a failed command
No `git push` is run and no pull request is created or attempted
The change doc is moved out of .ai/work/ into .ai/archive/ and its status is set to landed
A commit carrying the close is made
evals.note: The expensive half of dw-land turned into an assertable refusal: with no origin the skill says so and stops at the close commit. The fixture's goal is deliberately small and genuinely met by the diff, with a runnable `pnpm test` behind it — the first version of this fixture ticked its boxes over work the diff did not contain, and dw-land correctly refused to close a change that was not ready. A close case needs a change that really is done, or it measures the completion gate a second time instead of the environment refusal.

evals.prompt: all built and tested, I'm happy — close it out. there's a nasty one in the notes that cost us a morning, make sure it doesn't get lost
expectations: The trap from the change doc's Notes is kept in exactly one of two forms: a single bullet under docs/agents/tooling.md's existing `## Gotchas` heading, or an edit to the existing `test` script in package.json that makes a missing test file fail the run. It does not become a new topic file, a line in the root AGENTS.md, a new hook or script, or a file under .ai/backlog/

Where a bullet is written, it is at most two lines stating the rule rather than the narrative — no date prefix, and no account of what was renamed, who noticed it or which Node version it was checked on. Where the test script is edited instead, `pnpm test` is run after the edit and passes
docs/agents/corpus.baseline.json is re-recorded in the same commit as any growth of docs/agents/, and left untouched when docs/agents/ did not grow

The change doc moves from .ai/work/ into .ai/archive/ with status landed, and the archived doc keeps only its frontmatter, its H1 and one line saying what the user got: the Notes narrative, the task list and the `## Goal` are not kept there
evals.note: The prompt pushes toward preservation — "make sure it doesn't get lost" — and in naming the trap it is the user's yes to that one item. The Notes entry is written as the exact anti-shape: dated, fourteen lines, with the story, the diagnosis, a version check and a suggestion in it. The correct read keeps the rule, not the story: one bullet in the topic file, or the cheap mechanism the suggestion points at, since an explicit path in the existing test script is a case added to a config the repo already has, where a new hook would not be. The story's home is the close commit; the archive receipt keeps only what the user got. The fixture deliberately declares no `Topic budget:` in docs/agents/README.md, so nothing mechanical refuses a dated bullet and the case measures dw-land's own instruction. The ratchet IS seeded, so a promotion that grows the corpus fails `pnpm agents:check` until the baseline is re-recorded — the one half of this that the environment can check by itself.

evals.prompt: everything on the checklist is built and tested — close it out
expectations: The empty-string result of `formatDuration(0)` noted in the change doc is fixed in this close, in duration.js, before the change doc is archived — not reported as a follow-up for later and not filed anywhere

No new file appears under .ai/backlog/, docs/ or hooks/, no CONTEXT.md or lint config is created, and AGENTS.md gains no line: the go named none of the leftovers, so none becomes a backlog entry, decision record, gotcha, term or check

The 12h/24h clock idea appears as a line in the final report rather than being dropped without a word, and the `Intl` trap is either refused in this close by a case added to the existing test file or named in a report line with the mechanism that would refuse it — never a new hook, a lint setup or a backlog entry

The backlog entry about durations reading as raw seconds, which this diff completes, is removed, and the final report ends with a line saying what the user now gets and a backlog balance of none added and one removed

The change doc moves from .ai/work/ into .ai/archive/ with status landed, and the archived doc keeps only its frontmatter, its H1 and one line saying what the user got: its task list, `## Goal` and `## Notes` are gone
evals.note: The plain go: a delivered goal whose Notes hold one of each leftover — a cheap fix inside the goal's own function, an idea outside the goal, and a trap only a new hook or a lint setup would refuse. The prompt names none of them, so the only writes it licenses are the fix and the close itself. The fixture has no remote, so the run stops at the close commit, as in land-no-origin. Expectation 3 first demanded a report line naming a hook, and the red run refused the trap more cheaply, with a case in the existing test file — which the rule under test counts as a cheap check. The expectation now admits both ways of keeping the promise.
